complexity.notes: Clean and idiomatic; seeding d[None] = None to avoid None checks is a nice touch. The dict keys are node objects, whose identity hashes the input cannot steer, so lookups stay O(1) even in the worst case. An O(1)-extra-space variant exists that ||interleaves each copy directly after its original node, sets random pointers via original.random.next, then unweaves the two lists||.
complexity.summary: Two-pass deep copy: first pass builds a dict mapping each original node to a fresh node with its value, second pass wires up next and random pointers through the map. The d[None] = None sentinel lets null pointers resolve through the same lookup without special-casing.
